title: Pruning with the constraint that paths exclude 3
summary: When searching for root-to-7 paths that do not contain 3, return early at node 3 to prune its subtree, skipping node 6 and the right 7.
context: The binary tree has seven nodes: root 1 has left and right children 7 and 3; the left node 7 has left and right children 4 and 5; node 3 has left and right children 6 and another 7; nodes 4, 5, 6, and the right 7 are all leaf nodes.
The problem asks for paths from the root to all nodes with value 7 such that no path contains a node with value 3. Any path extending downward past node 3 necessarily violates this constraint.
description: The left subtree contains no 3, so preorder traversal records the valid path [1, 7] upon visiting the left node 7 and continues checking its children 4 and 5.

Reaching the root's right child 3 triggers the constraint, so the algorithm returns immediately before appending 3 to path and does not recurse into its children 6 and the right 7. The figure marks node 3 in red and uses a scissors icon with a faded subtree to show that this search branch is skipped; the tree nodes themselves are not deleted from the data structure.

frames.title: Return early at node 3 to prune the invalid search branch
frames.explanation: The only path satisfying the constraint is [1, 7]. Although the right leaf node 7 equals the target value 7, the path [1, 3, 7] from the root to it passes through the forbidden node 3 and is therefore ruled out during pruning.
